hero.text: Nova carried the fragile glass statue with both hands so it would not crack.

everyday: The box said FRAGILE, so we carried the dishes inside very carefully.

contrast.nonExample: Sam's rubber ball bounced off the brick wall without a single scratch.
contrast.explanation: Fragile things break easily. The rubber ball is tough and bouncy, so it is sturdy, not fragile.

items.prompt: Is the egg fragile?
items.passage: A bird's egg can crack if you squeeze it even a little.
items.hint: Does the egg break easily?
items.explanation: Fragile means easily broken. An egg that cracks with a small squeeze is fragile.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: Be gentle with the butterfly, because its thin wings are very ___.
items.hint: Why do you need to be gentle with thin wings?
items.explanation: "Be gentle" and "thin wings" show the wings could tear easily. That is fragile.

items.prompt: Which word is closest in meaning to "fragile" in this sentence?
items.passage: The old book had fragile pages that tore when you touched them.
items.hint: The pages tore when touched.
items.explanation: Delicate means easily damaged, like fragile. Pages that tear at a touch are delicate.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what fragile means.

chunks.text: so we could kick it around.

items.hint: Fragile things need protection.
items.explanation: You wrap a fragile vase so it won't break. Kicking a fragile vase would smash it.

items.prompt: Which word best describes the teacups?
items.passage: Grandma's teacups are so thin that even a small bump could chip them.
items.clue: so thin; even a small bump could chip them
items.hint: What could happen with just a small bump?
items.explanation: "Even a small bump could chip them" shows the cups break easily. That is fragile. Sturdy is the opposite.

definition: happy to give or share, often more than you have to

hero.text: Bolt was generous and gave half of his snack to a hungry kid in the park.

everyday: Our generous neighbor shares tomatoes from her garden with the whole street.

contrast.nonExample: Ollie kept all the crayons in a pile and would not let anyone use them.
contrast.explanation: Generous people share and give freely. Ollie kept everything for himself, so he was selfish.

items.prompt: Which person is generous?

options.text: Ruby keeps every cookie for herself and hides the jar.
Ruby shares her cookies with the whole class.
Ruby counts her cookies and eats one.

items.hint: Who gives to others?
items.explanation: Generous means happy to give and share. Ruby shares with the whole class.

wrong.a: Hiding the jar is selfish, the opposite of generous.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: It was ___ of Marco to give his old bike to his little cousin.
items.clue: give his old bike to his little cousin
items.hint: What kind of person gives away a bike?
items.explanation: Giving his bike to his cousin is a kind act of giving. That is generous.

items.prompt: Which word means the OPPOSITE of "generous" in this sentence?
items.passage: The generous baker gave free bread to everyone in line.
items.hint: Which person would NOT give bread away?
items.explanation: Selfish people keep things for themselves, the opposite of generous people who give.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what generous means.

chunks.text: his umbrella with a friend in the rain.
nothing and kept his umbrella to himself.

items.hint: Generous people share.
items.explanation: Sharing his umbrella is generous. Keeping it to himself is the opposite.

items.prompt: Which word best describes Mia?
items.passage: Mia gave away ten of her twelve toys to children who had none.
items.clue: gave away ten of her twelve toys
items.hint: Mia is not just using good manners. What is she doing?
items.explanation: Giving away most of her toys is giving freely, which is generous. Polite is about good manners, like saying please, not about giving.

wrong.a: Polite means having good manners. Mia is giving a lot away, which is generous.

hero.text: Pixel glanced at her watch and saw she had one minute to reach the bank.

everyday: During the test, Ana glanced at the clock and then went back to work.

contrast.nonExample: Owen stared at the painting for ten minutes, studying every color.
contrast.explanation: A glance is quick. Owen looked for a long time, so he stared or studied it.

items.prompt: Did Ken glance at the map?
items.passage: Ken looked at the map for a long time, tracing every road with his finger.
items.hint: Was Ken's look quick or long?
items.explanation: To glance is to look quickly. Ken looked for a long time, so he studied the map instead.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: Before crossing the street, Ava ___ quickly to the left and right.
items.clue: quickly to the left and right
items.hint: What do you do with your eyes before crossing?
items.explanation: "Quickly" and "left and right" show Ava took fast looks. That is glancing.

items.prompt: Which word means the OPPOSITE of "glanced" in this sentence?
items.passage: Dad glanced at the newspaper headline before running out the door.
items.hint: A glance is short. What is a long look called?
items.explanation: Stared means looked for a long time, the opposite of a quick glance. Peeked is close in meaning to glanced.

wrong.a: Peeked is a quick look too, so it is close in meaning, not opposite.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what glance means.

chunks.text: for just a second before she ordered.
for a whole hour before she ordered.

items.hint: A glance is very short.
items.explanation: A glance lasts about a second. Looking for a whole hour is not a glance.

items.prompt: Which word best tells what the goalie did?
items.passage: The goalie took one quick look over her shoulder just before the ball came.
items.hint: Was her look long and careful, or fast?
items.explanation: "One quick look" is a glance. Observed would mean watching carefully for a while.

wrong.a: Observing is careful watching over time. The goalie only took one quick look.

definition: happening slowly, a little at a time

hero.text: Juniper's power made a gradual glow that grew brighter, little by little, until the cave was lit.

everyday: The gradual change of the leaves from green to red took several weeks.

contrast.nonExample: All the lights in the house went off at once when the power failed.
contrast.explanation: Gradual changes happen slowly, step by step. The lights went off all at once, so the change was sudden.

items.prompt: What does "gradual" mean in this sentence?
items.passage: There was a gradual rise in the river after days of light rain.

options.text: sudden and very fast, all at once
slow, a little at a time

items.hint: Light rain for days would make the river rise how?
items.explanation: Gradual means slow and a little at a time. Days of light rain raised the river slowly.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: The puppy's growth was ___, so we never noticed it getting bigger each day.
items.clue: never noticed it getting bigger each day
items.hint: Why wouldn't you notice a change each day?
items.explanation: You don't notice a change each day when it happens slowly, a little at a time. That is gradual.

items.prompt: Which word means the OPPOSITE of "gradual" in this sentence?
items.passage: The hill had a gradual slope that was easy to walk up.
items.hint: A gradual slope rises slowly. What kind of slope rises sharply?
items.explanation: A gradual slope goes up a little at a time. A steep slope goes up sharply, the opposite. Gentle means almost the same as gradual here.

wrong.a: Gentle is close in meaning to gradual for a hill, not opposite.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what gradual means.

chunks.text: getting a little taller each week.

items.hint: Gradual means little by little.
items.explanation: Growing a little each week is gradual. Shooting up overnight is sudden.

items.prompt: Is this a gradual change?
items.passage: A balloon popped with a loud bang in less than one second.
items.hint: Did it happen slowly or all at once?
items.explanation: Gradual changes happen slowly. A pop in less than a second is sudden, not gradual.

definition: the natural home of an animal or plant

hero.text: Kai helped rebuild the frogs' pond habitat after the flood washed it away.

everyday: A polar bear's habitat is cold and icy, with lots of snow and sea.

contrast.nonExample: The grocery store is where we go to buy milk and bread.
contrast.explanation: A habitat is the natural place where a plant or animal lives and finds what it needs. A store is a place people visit to shop, not a natural home.

items.prompt: Which is a habitat?

options.text: the desert where a camel lives
the store where we buy milk
the bus that takes us to school

items.hint: Which is the natural home of an animal?
items.explanation: A habitat is the natural place an animal lives. The desert is a camel's habitat.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: Cutting down the forest destroyed the owls' ___.
items.hint: What is a forest to the owls who live there?
items.explanation: The forest is where the owls live naturally, so it is their habitat.

items.prompt: What is the desert for cactuses?
items.passage: Cactuses grow well in the hot, dry desert, where there is lots of sun and little rain.
items.clue: grow well in the hot, dry desert
items.hint: Where do cactuses live and grow?
items.explanation: "Grow well in the hot, dry desert" shows the desert is where cactuses naturally live. That is their habitat.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what habitat means.

chunks.text: because it gives them food and shelter.
because it has a big parking lot.

items.hint: A habitat gives living things what they need.
items.explanation: A habitat provides food and shelter. A parking lot does not help birds live.

items.prompt: Is the rainforest the monkeys' habitat?
items.passage: Monkeys live high in the trees of the rainforest, where they find fruit and stay safe.
items.hint: Do the monkeys live there and find what they need?
items.explanation: The monkeys live in the rainforest and find food and safety there, so it is their habitat.

definition: to copy the way someone looks, acts, or sounds

hero.text: Rex imitated the villain's deep voice so well that the guards opened the gate.

everyday: My little brother imitates everything I do, even the way I tie my shoes.

contrast.nonExample: Zoe made up a brand-new dance that nobody had ever seen before.
contrast.explanation: To imitate is to copy someone else. Zoe created something new, so she was inventing, not imitating.

items.prompt: Is the parrot imitating its owner?
items.passage: A parrot says "Hello!" in the very same voice as its owner.
items.hint: Is the parrot copying how someone sounds?
items.explanation: To imitate is to copy. The parrot copies its owner's voice.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: The baby tried to ___ the funny sounds her father made.
items.clue: the funny sounds her father made
items.hint: Babies learn to talk by doing what?
items.explanation: The baby tries to make the same sounds as her father. Copying sounds is imitating.

items.prompt: Which word is closest in meaning to "imitated" in this sentence?
items.passage: The students imitated the artist's brushstrokes to learn her style.
items.hint: How do you learn someone's style?
items.explanation: Copied means the same as imitated. The students made brushstrokes just like the artist's.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what imitate means.

chunks.text: "meow" and licked the back of his hand.

items.hint: To imitate a cat, you copy what a cat does.
items.explanation: Meowing and licking like a cat copies a cat. Barking and wagging copies a dog instead.

items.prompt: Which line uses "imitate" correctly?

options.text: "I will imitate a new song that no one has ever heard."
"Watch me imitate how a penguin walks!"
"Please imitate the box onto the top shelf."

items.hint: Imitating means copying something that already exists.
items.explanation: Walking like a penguin copies a penguin, so it is imitating. You can't copy a song no one has heard, and you can't imitate a box onto a shelf.

definition: wild and rushed because of fear or worry

hero.text: Bolt made a frantic search for the lost child as the crowd grew bigger.

everyday: Mom was frantic when she couldn't find her car keys and we were already late.

contrast.nonExample: Jen calmly packed her bag for the trip while humming a song.
contrast.explanation: Frantic means rushed and worried. Jen was calm and relaxed, so she was not frantic.

items.prompt: Which person is frantic?

options.text: Ray sits on a soft blanket and reads quietly under a shady tree.
Ray runs around yelling, "Where is my dog? I can't find him!"

items.hint: Who is rushing around in a worried way?
items.explanation: Frantic means wild and rushed with worry. Ray runs and yells because he can't find his dog.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: When the bees flew into the tent, the ___ campers ran around waving their arms.
items.hint: How do people act when bees surprise them?
items.explanation: "Ran around waving their arms" shows wild, scared rushing. That is frantic.

items.prompt: Which word means the OPPOSITE of "frantic" in this sentence?
items.passage: We made a frantic dash to the bus stop before the bus pulled away.
items.hint: Frantic is wild and worried. What is the opposite feeling?
items.explanation: Calm is relaxed and steady, the opposite of frantic. Quick describes speed, and a frantic dash is quick too.

wrong.a: A frantic dash is quick, so quick is not the opposite.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what frantic means.

chunks.text: and stretched out for a peaceful nap.

items.hint: Frantic animals rush around in fear.
items.explanation: Dashing under the bed is a scared, rushed action, so it shows frantic. A peaceful nap is calm.

items.prompt: Which word best describes Ava?
items.passage: Late for the bus, Ava ran around the kitchen grabbing papers and dropping her pencil.
items.clue: Late; ran around grabbing papers and dropping her pencil
items.hint: How is Ava moving, and why?
items.explanation: Being late and running around grabbing and dropping things shows wild, worried rushing. That is frantic.

hero.text: Nova was furious when the thief smashed the museum window, and her eyes blazed.

everyday: Dad was furious when someone dumped trash all over our clean yard.

contrast.nonExample: Jo frowned a little when the tip of her pencil broke.
contrast.explanation: Furious means very, very angry. A small frown over a broken pencil is only a little annoyed.

items.prompt: What does "furious" mean in this sentence?
items.passage: The farmer was furious when the goats ate his whole garden.
items.hint: How would you feel if goats ate your WHOLE garden?
items.explanation: Furious means extremely angry. Losing the whole garden would make the farmer very angry.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: Kim was ___ when her little brother broke her new tablet on purpose.
items.clue: broke her new tablet on purpose
items.hint: How would someone feel if their new thing was broken on purpose?
items.explanation: Breaking something new "on purpose" would make Kim extremely angry. That is furious.

items.prompt: Which word best describes how Kai felt?
items.passage: Someone stomped on Kai's sandcastle on purpose. Kai's face turned red and he yelled as loud as he could.
items.clue: face turned red; yelled as loud as he could
items.hint: Is Kai a little angry or extremely angry?
items.explanation: A red face and yelling as loud as he could show extreme anger, so furious fits. Annoyed is only a little angry, which is too weak here.

wrong.a: Annoyed means a little bothered. Kai's red face and loud yelling show much stronger anger.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what furious means.

chunks.text: when he saw his broken window,

items.hint: Furious people show strong anger.
items.explanation: Stomping and shouting show extreme anger, so they fit furious. Smiling and humming show happiness.

items.prompt: Which word is closest in meaning to "furious" in this sentence?
items.passage: The furious bull snorted and charged at the fence.
items.hint: Snorting and charging show a strong feeling.
items.explanation: Enraged means filled with rage, or extremely angry, just like furious. Gentle is the opposite.

definition: feeling thankful for something someone did or gave

hero.text: The family was grateful that Juniper rescued their cat, so they baked her a pie.

everyday: I was grateful when my friend helped me carry my heavy backpack home.

contrast.nonExample: Liam got a new sweater as a gift and complained that it was the wrong color.
contrast.explanation: Grateful people feel and show thanks. Liam complained instead of being thankful.

items.prompt: Is Ana grateful?
items.passage: After Ms. Park helped Ana with her reading, Ana made her a thank-you card.
items.hint: What does a thank-you card show?
items.explanation: Grateful means thankful. Ana shows her thanks with a card.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: We were ___ to the firefighters who saved our neighbor's home.
items.clue: the firefighters who saved our neighbor's home
items.hint: How do you feel toward someone who helps?
items.explanation: The firefighters saved a home, so people would feel thankful to them. That is grateful.

items.prompt: Which word is closest in meaning to "grateful" in this sentence?
items.passage: The tired hikers were grateful for the cool water.
items.hint: How does a tired hiker feel about getting water?
items.explanation: Thankful means the same as grateful. The hikers were thankful for the water.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what grateful means.

chunks.text: but grumbled that fishing was boring.

items.hint: Grateful people say thanks and mean it.
items.explanation: Thanking her grandpa for teaching her shows gratitude. Grumbling that it was boring does not.

items.prompt: Which line shows someone being grateful?

options.text: "You finally fixed my bike? It took way too long, and it still squeaks."
"Thank you for fixing my bike! I really needed it."
"My bike is red and has two wheels."

items.hint: Which speaker says thanks?
items.explanation: Saying thank you and "I really needed it" shows thankfulness. That is grateful. The first speaker complains instead.

definition: normal and usual; not special or different

hero.text: Pixel looked like an ordinary student at her desk, but she was secretly a hero.

everyday: It was an ordinary Tuesday: breakfast, school, homework, and bed.

contrast.nonExample: On parade day, a giant balloon dragon floated down Main Street.
contrast.explanation: Ordinary means plain and usual. A giant balloon dragon is special and unusual, not ordinary.

items.prompt: Which is ordinary?

options.text: a purple elephant that can talk
a sparrow hopping on the sidewalk
a snowman in the middle of summer

items.hint: Which one could you see on any normal day?
items.explanation: Ordinary means normal and usual. A sparrow on the sidewalk is something you see every day.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: The rock looked ___ on the outside, but inside it had sparkling purple crystals.
items.clue: but inside it had sparkling purple crystals
items.hint: "But" shows a surprise. The inside was special, so the outside was...?
items.explanation: "But" sets up a contrast with the special crystals inside. The outside was plain and normal, or ordinary.

items.prompt: Which word means the OPPOSITE of "ordinary" in this sentence?
items.passage: Lunch was just an ordinary cheese sandwich and an apple.
items.hint: Ordinary means normal. What is the opposite?
items.explanation: Unusual means not normal, the opposite of ordinary. Usual means the same as ordinary.

wrong.a: Usual is a synonym of ordinary, not its opposite.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what ordinary means.
items.hint: If nothing special happens, what kind of day is it?
items.explanation: A day when nothing special happens is ordinary. An amazing, surprising day is not ordinary.

items.prompt: Which word best describes the party?
items.passage: Ty expected a fancy party, but it was just pizza and games like every other weekend.
items.clue: just pizza and games like every other weekend
items.hint: Was the party special or like always?
items.explanation: "Just" and "like every other weekend" show the party was normal and usual. That is ordinary. Peculiar means strange, the opposite.
